decisions.reason: The path-product definition is sound, but its concluding across-step independence wording conflates independent random innovations with resulting states. With L=1, N=3 and alpha=(1,2/3,1/3,0), P(Z1=m,Z2=m)=1/3 differs from P(Z1=m)P(Z2=m)=2/9. This is a nonfatal explanatory defect: the explicit kernel/path law and all coordinate-path independence properties are unchanged. Replaced it by independence of coordinate trajectories given X and next-coordinate states given the preceding state. The judge N=2 example alone is inconclusive because Z2=m is deterministic.

The mathematical Statement and proof correctly identify E[-E(X)] with the weighted conditional cross-entropy, not E(x) itself. The title omits both negation and data averaging, a nonfatal presentation defect. Corrected the title and owning manifest title mirror without changing any Statement or proof.

The cited item is a counterexample and its universal factorization sentence is expressly headed Statement refuted. Its complete argument puts probability 1/2 on each of 00 and 11 given the certain all-mask state, while the product of marginals puts 1/4 on 01. It therefore supports the remark rather than contradicting it. The remark correctly restricts the ELBO endpoint cancellation to exact endpoints and asserts no continuum or estimator-variance theorem. Sahoo sections 3.2.3, 3.3 and B.1.1-B.1.3 confirm the terminology attribution; no item edit is needed.
